1004672.etyen:
Variant of Solveig, from Old Norse Sǫlveig. The first element is traditionally connected with salr (“hall, house”), while the second element -veig probably means “strength, ability” or “fighter, warrior”.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Solvei, Swedish Solvei and Danish Solvei (“female given name”).

Finland was a grand principality, with the Russian emperor as grand prince, from 1809 to 1917.

1004928.etyen:
From storfyrste (“grand prince”) + -dømme (“domain, area of rule”), literally “domain of a grand prince”.
The base storfyrste (“grand prince”) is formed from stor (“great”) and fyrste (“prince”). The former is from Old Norse stórr (“big, great”), from Proto-Germanic *stōraz (“big, large”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to stand”). The latter is borrowed from Middle Low German vurste (“prince; first”), from Proto-Germanic *furistaz (“first, foremost”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- (“before”). The suffix -dømme (“domain, area of rule or power”) is from Old Norse dǿ
